feature: Upload guards: size caps, concurrency, SSRF

error_found: Bad archive returns 500 instead of 400: POST /api/v1/batch with a non-ZIP payload named .zip (STL bytes, application/zip) -> HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error' (reproduced twice). Cause: batch_service.extract_zip_path_to_items opens zipfile.ZipFile which raises zipfile.BadZipFile; batch_router.py only catches ValueError around extraction, so BadZipFile escapes as an unhandled 500. Expected 400 per story.
notes: Non-ZIP bytes named .zip -> 400 BAD_REQUEST 'File is not a zip file', no orphaned batch. 9.9MB manifest -> 413 BATCH_MANIFEST_TOO_LARGE (2MiB cap) live. concurrency_limit=99 -> 422 INVALID_BATCH_CONCURRENCY {min:1,max:12}. webhook_url=169.254.169.254 -> 400 webhook_url_rejected (SSRF). 5GiB declared/streamed ZIP 413 code-verified only (batch_router.py:234-256; multipart parse precedes the endpoint check so a spoofed Content-Length without a real multi-GiB body cannot reach it).

expected: No auth; IP rate limit 120/hour (429). 200 returns sanitized analysis data with X-Robots-Tag: noindex and Cache-Control: private, no-store headers; 404 for unknown, revoked, or expired short ids.
notes: Unauthenticated 200 with X-Robots-Tag: noindex and Cache-Control: private, no-store; sanitized body (verdict/geometry/process_scores/priority_fixes only - no email or key material). 404 for unknown short id and for revoked share. 120/hr IP 429 untested.

story: As a viewer, I want to page through my organization's past analyses and open one with its full result and linked cost decisions so I can revisit prior work.
expected: Viewer role (401 no key), 60/hour;500/day (429). List is org-scoped via caller_org_subquery (never leaks other orgs), cursor-paginated by ULID desc (limit 1..100, default 20; 422 outside range), optional verdict filter (pass|issues|fail; invalid values silently ignored); returns {analyses, next_cursor, has_more}. Detail returns full result_json plus is_public/share_url and up to 20 decision_links matched by org+mesh_hash; 404 for unknown or other-org ULIDs.
notes: 401 no key. List {analyses, next_cursor, has_more}, ULID-desc, cursor present; limit=0 and limit=101 -> 422; verdict=pass returns only pass rows; invalid verdict silently ignored (200). Org scoping: fresh other-org key 404s on my analysis detail and its own list is empty. Detail includes full result_json, is_public/share_url, decision_links matched by org+mesh_hash (cost decision linked to the qa-box analysis). 404 unknown ULID.

feature: Async job status polling and result fetch
story: As an API engineer, I want to poll an async job (e.g. SAM-3D) and fetch its result when done so I can complete long-running workflows.
expected: Viewer role (401 no key). Status returns {job_id, status, job_type, timestamps, result_url, error}; result_url is set only when status is done/partial, and error carries {code, message} (JOB_FAILED fallback) when failed. Both endpoints return 404 for non-existent jobs AND other users' jobs (no existence leak); /result also 404s ('Job result not yet available') while the job is queued/running.
notes: 401 no key. Status: {job_id, status:partial, job_type:sam3d, created/started/completed timestamps, result_url set, error:null}; /result 200 {job_id, status, result}. 404 for non-existent job, malformed job id, AND another user's job (no existence leak). Failed-job error shape and queued-state /result 404 untested (job completed instantly).

story: As an operator, I want a health endpoint that never claims an absent dependency is healthy so my monitors reflect reality.
expected: No auth. 200 {status: ok} only when Postgres probe passes and (when the async tier is expected: real REDIS_URL or RELEASE set, with ASYNC_STRICT_HEALTH=1 default) Redis is reachable; otherwise 503 {status: degraded}. Body always reports real probes: postgres, redis, async{redis, worker: ok|unknown|unavailable, expected}, reconstruction{available, backend, egress}, version, build_id. Worker 'unknown' (no arq heartbeat key) does not gate status unless WORKER_STRICT_HEALTH=1.
notes: 200 {status:ok} with real probes: postgres:true, redis:true, async{redis:true, worker:'ok', expected:true, worker_strict:false}, reconstruction{available:false, backend:'none', egress:false} (honest), version, build_id. Single 'server: ProofShape' header. 503 degraded path untestable (cannot take deps down).

feature: Deep dependency health with optional token gate
story: As an operator, I want per-dependency probes (Postgres, Redis, worker heartbeat age, queue depth, object store) so I can diagnose exactly what is degraded.
expected: When DEEP_HEALTH_TOKEN is set (or PRODUCTION_DEEP_HEALTH_AUTH_REQUIRED=1), a missing/wrong X-CadVerify-Health-Token returns 404 'Not found' (hides the endpoint, not 401). Otherwise 200/503 with checks.postgres{ok,error}, checks.redis{ok,expected,configured,error}, checks.worker{state: ok|stale|unknown|unavailable, heartbeat_age_seconds, stale_threshold_seconds}, checks.queue{depth,name}, checks.object_store{ok,expected,backend}; 503 when Postgres down, expected Redis unreachable (strict), strict worker not ok, or expected object store failing healthcheck. Worker state is never fabricated 'ok' without a fresh heartbeat.
notes: DEEP_HEALTH_TOKEN unset -> endpoint open: 200 without and with a wrong X-CadVerify-Health-Token. All documented fields present: checks.postgres{ok,error}, checks.redis{ok,expected,configured,error}, checks.worker{state:'ok', heartbeat_age_seconds:12, stale_threshold_seconds:90}, checks.queue{depth:3, name:'arq:queue'}, checks.object_store{ok:false, expected:false, backend:'local'} - failing-but-unexpected store correctly does not gate status. Token-gated 404 path untestable here (dev-flag state).

feature: Structured error responses with stable codes
story: As an API consumer, I want every error to carry a stable machine-readable code, message, and doc_url so I can handle failures programmatically.
expected: Any HTTPException is wrapped as {code, message, doc_url[, detail]} using the stable map (400 BAD_REQUEST, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, 403 FORBIDDEN, 404 NOT_FOUND, 409 CONFLICT, 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE, 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, 429 RATE_LIMITED, 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED, 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, 504 ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT). A detail dict already containing 'code' (e.g. GEOMETRY_INVALID, SAM3D_ENQUEUE_FAILED) passes through unchanged with original headers; Pydantic validation failures return 422 VALIDATION_ERROR.
notes: Every error observed carried {code, message, doc_url}: BAD_REQUEST (bad params/files), NOT_FOUND (unknown route + resources), FILE_TOO_LARGE (demo 413), VALIDATION_ERROR (extra_forbidden, missing fields, limit out of range), plus passthrough detail codes preserved unchanged: auth_missing (401), GEOMETRY_INVALID (400 with geometry payload), DIRECT_UPLOAD_INVALID_PURPOSE/INVALID_CHECKSUM/IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED/NOT_FOUND/REQUIRES_S3 (422/404/501), rate_limited (429 with Retry-After:3600). The pass-1 plain-text 500 regression is gone (unsupported-suffix re-upload now clean 400 envelope). 409/503/504 codes not triggered.

story: As a holder of an old docs link, I want /docs to forward me so that I land on the current API quickstart.
expected: /docs unconditionally issues a Next.js redirect to /developers; no content is rendered at /docs itself.
notes: curl: 307 redirect to /developers; browser navigation to /docs lands on /developers with no content rendered at /docs.

story: As an analyst, I confirm/correct a part's declared identity so future retrievals carry a human assertion instead of a guess.
expected: Analyst role required; upserts declared_part_id/name/program onto the (org, mesh_hash) corpus row with source='user_confirmed' and emits identity.confirm audit event. 400 if caller has no org, mesh_hash blank, or no declared field supplied; 404 if the mesh has no corpus row in the caller's org (incl. another org's part — never a cross-tenant write, never a fabricated signature). Rate-limited 120/hour.
notes: Confirm upserts declared fields with source=user_confirmed (200); 400 blank mesh_hash; 400 no declared field; 404 unknown mesh; 404 cross-org write attempt (other org's mesh_hash); 403 for platform-viewer caller. identity.confirm audit event visible in org audit log.

story: As an analyst, I bulk-upload my org's CAD library (files or ZIP) with an identity mapping so the corpus has real declared identities on day one.
expected: Analyst role + kill-switch open required; 403 if no org. Accepts multipart files and/or ZIP plus optional CSV/JSON mapping; 400 if no files, 413 if >512MB (env PARTS_MASTER_MAX_MB) or over ONBOARD_MAX_FILES cap, 400 if mapping is not UTF-8. Returns honest summary {onboarded, skipped:[{filename,reason}], mapping_errors, library_size} — unparseable files are skipped, never abort the batch; missing names onboard bare geometry with no guessing. Rate-limited 20/hour.
notes: Onboarded 2 STLs + mapping CSV: honest summary {onboarded:2, skipped:[qa-fake.stl with reason], mapping_errors:[], library_size:2}; unparseable file skipped without aborting batch; 400 no files; 400 non-UTF-8 mapping; 403 viewer role. 413 >512MB / ONBOARD_MAX_FILES cap not exercised (impractical upload size), all other documented paths verified.

story: As a viewer, I see my org's identity-corpus size and recent entries, and download the mapping CSV contract.
expected: Viewer role required. GET /library returns {library_size, recent:[...]} org-scoped with declared identity only (raw signature vector never emitted); 403 if caller has no org. GET /library/template returns text/csv with header 'filename' (required) + optional part_id/name/program/material_class and needs no org.
notes: GET /library returns {library_size, recent} org-scoped, declared identity only (no raw signature vector in payload); viewer role allowed and sees only own org (empty for fresh org). Template is text/csv with filename + part_id/name/program/material_class columns.

story: As an analyst, I create a named org and become its admin.
expected: Analyst role + kill-switch open required; 201 with {org_id, name, slug, org_role:'admin'}; caller's active org is NOT auto-switched. 400 for empty name or name >200 chars. Emits org.created audit event.
notes: 201 {org_id,name,slug,org_role:admin}; active org NOT auto-switched (verified via GET /orgs is_active flags); 400 empty name; 400 name >200 chars; 403 platform-viewer.

story: As a viewer, I list every org I belong to and see which is active.
expected: Viewer role required; returns caller's memberships with the active org flagged; no cross-user data.
notes: Returns caller memberships with active_org_id + is_active flags; second user sees only own orgs (no cross-user data).

story: As a member with a dashboard session, I switch my active org.
expected: Viewer role + kill-switch open; org-bound API keys are refused with 403 {code:'api_key_org_bound'} — only dashboard sessions may switch (keys are permanently org-bound). 403 'not a member of that organization' when switching to an org without membership. Emits org.switched.
notes: API key switch refused 403 {code:api_key_org_bound}; dashboard-session switch succeeds (200 with new org); switch to non-member org 403 'not a member of that organization'.

story: As an org admin, I manage SAML group-to-role mappings for JIT provisioning in my org.
expected: Org-admin role required (mutations kill-switch gated); mappings are strictly org-scoped — list returns only caller-org rows, delete of another org's mapping fails. POST returns 201 with serialized mapping; both mutations emit saml.group_mapping.* audit events.
notes: POST 201 with serialized mapping (org roles admin/member/viewer; invalid role 400); list strictly org-scoped (other org sees empty); cross-org DELETE of mapping id returns 404; org-admin required.

story: As an org admin, I invite an email at a role and review my org's invites.
expected: Org-admin required; invited role may not exceed the inviter's (403). POST returns 201 with the one-time accept_link exactly once (token stored only as hash, never persisted raw) and emailed flag; email send is best-effort — missing RESEND config or send failure never breaks invite creation. GET lists org invites (pending/accepted/expired/revoked) with no tokens. Invite creation rate-limited 20/hour.
notes: POST 201 returns accept_link exactly once + emailed:false (no RESEND config, creation unaffected); GET lists invites with statuses and no tokens; non-admin org member gets 403; 21st invite in the hour hit the 20/hour limit (429) per ID-036 test. Inviter is always org-admin (top org role) so 'role exceeds inviter' 403 is not reachable via this route.

story: As an invited user, I redeem the one-time token to join the org at the invited role.
expected: Any authed user (viewer+), kill-switch gated; token is hash-compared and single-use. 400 empty token; 404 unknown/used token; 409 revoked, already-used, or expired; 403 if the invite was issued to a different account/email. Accepting never escalates an existing member's role; returns {org_id, org_role, created} and emits member.joined only when a membership is created.
notes: Accept 200 {org_id, org_role, created:true}; 400 empty token; 404 unknown token; 409 replay (already used); 409 revoked token; 403 token issued to a different account; re-invite of existing member at admin role returned created:false and did NOT escalate (member kept).

story: As an org admin, I revoke a pending invite so the link stops working.
expected: Org-admin required, kill-switch gated, org-scoped: 404 if the invite is absent (or belongs to another org), 409 if already accepted; returns the serialized invite with revoked state.
notes: Revoke returns serialized invite status=revoked; revoked link then 409 on accept; 404 unknown id and 404 for another org's invite id; 409 revoking an accepted invite.

story: As any org member (viewer+), I see my org's members and their org roles.
expected: Org viewer role required; returns only the caller's active org's members — no cross-org leakage; 403 if the caller has no org.
notes: Org viewer can list; returns only caller's active org members (org A: admin/member/viewer; other org key sees only its own single member) - no cross-org leakage.

story: As an org admin, I change a member's org role.
expected: Org-admin required, kill-switch gated; 404 if the target is not a member of this org; 409 when demoting the last admin (an org must keep at least one admin). Emits member.role_changed and returns {user_id, org_role}.
notes: Admin promoted viewer->member (200 {user_id, org_role}); 404 target not a member; 409 demoting the last admin; 403 non-admin caller.

story: As an org admin I remove a member, or as any member I leave the org myself.
expected: Route accepts org viewer, but a non-admin removing anyone other than themselves gets 403 {code:'insufficient_org_role'} — self-leave only. 404 if target not a member; 409 if the last admin would be removed or leave. Removal is org-scoped (not account deactivation) and takes effect immediately via membership re-validation; emits member.left/member.removed.
notes: Non-admin removing another member: 403 {code:insufficient_org_role}; self-leave 200 and the leaver's org-bound API key was rejected 401 immediately after; 404 non-member target; 409 last-admin removal; leaver's account still active in other org (org-scoped removal, not deactivation).

story: As an org admin I list and inspect only my org's users; as a superadmin I see all users platform-wide.
expected: require_org_role(admin): org-admin results are bounded by an INNER JOIN on memberships to ctx.org_id; a user outside the org returns 404 on detail so cross-org existence never leaks. Superadmin sees every user with primary (oldest) membership enriched. List is cursor-paginated (limit 1-100, next_cursor/has_more); detail includes org_role, auth_provider, analysis_count, batch_count.
notes: Org-admin list bounded to own org (only org members returned); detail of out-of-org user 404 (no existence leak); superadmin paginated platform-wide (limit=2 -> next_cursor + has_more:true); detail includes org_role, auth_provider, analysis_count, batch_count; 403 for org member.

story: As a platform superadmin, I change a user's global platform role.
expected: Superadmin only: an org-admin gets 403 {code:'platform_superadmin_required'} (org admins manage org_role on the org router, never users.role). 400 changing own role or role not in {viewer, analyst, admin} — 'superadmin' is deliberately not assignable via API; 404 unknown user. Emits user.role_changed with old/new roles.
notes: Org-admin 403 {code:platform_superadmin_required}; 400 changing own role; 400 role 'superadmin' not assignable; 404 unknown user; valid change 200 and reversible.

story: As a platform superadmin, I deactivate a compromised/offboarded account and later reactivate it.
expected: Superadmin only (deliberately not org-admin — deactivation is account-level and blocks EVERY auth path: login, Google/SAML/magic re-provision, existing sessions, API keys). Deactivate: 400 on self, 404 unknown user; flips is_active, sets deactivated_at, and bumps session_version so existing dashboard sessions die immediately. Reactivate reverses it; both idempotent (session_version only bumps on actual state change) and audited.
notes: Org-admin 403; 400 self-deactivate; 404 unknown user. Deactivate blocked API key (403 account_deactivated), killed existing dashboard session (403), and blocked login (403). Idempotent re-deactivate did not bump session_version; reactivate restored key + login (session_version bumped on real state change only).

story: As a platform superadmin, I invalidate every dashboard session for an account without deactivating it.
expected: Superadmin only; 404 unknown user. Bumps users.session_version so every existing dashboard cookie is invalidated on next validation while API keys and the account remain active; returns the new session_version and emits user.sessions_revoked.
notes: Superadmin only (org-admin 403); 404 unknown user; returns new session_version; existing dashboard session became 401 immediately while the user's org-bound API key kept working (initial 403 seen was api_key_org_mismatch from an active-org switch, unrelated to revocation) and account stayed active.

story: As an org admin, I see real usage counts for my org's trailing window.
expected: Org-admin required; days param 1-90 (default 30). Returns separate honest counts (analyses, cost_decisions, usage_events, webhook_deliveries) plus per-event-type and per-webhook-status breakdowns from persisted tables — never invented aggregate numbers. Org-admin counts are filtered to ctx.org_id; superadmin is unfiltered (org_id null in response).
notes: Org-admin gets org-filtered honest zero counts (analyses/cost_decisions/usage_events/webhook_deliveries) + breakdown maps; days 0 and 91 rejected (422); superadmin unfiltered with org_id:null; 403 for org member.

story: As an org admin, I inspect recent webhook delivery attempts and retry timing.
expected: Org-admin required; latest deliveries (limit 1-100) joined to batch ULID, org-scoped unless superadmin. Response contains status/attempts/response_code/retry timestamps but deliberately NEVER the payload body.
notes: Org-scoped (fresh org sees []); superadmin sees platform deliveries joined to batch_ulid with status/attempts/response_code/retry timestamps and NO payload body field; limit=101 rejected (422).

story: As an org admin/operator, I check async queue, batch, webhook, and worker posture.
expected: Org-admin required; returns PII-free summary scoped to the caller's org (superadmin sees platform-wide, org filter None).
notes: Org-admin gets PII-free async/jobs/batches/batch_items/webhooks summary scoped to own org_id; 403 for org member.

story: As an org admin, I query or CSV-export my org's audit trail for compliance.
expected: Org-admin required; start/end ISO datetimes mandatory (400 on invalid) with a hard 90-day max range (400 above). Org-admin sees only their org's entries, superadmin all orgs. format=csv returns text/csv attachment; default JSON is cursor-paginated (limit 1-200) with optional user_id/action filters.
notes: start/end mandatory (422 missing, 400 invalid datetime); 400 range >90 days; org-admin sees only own-org-relevant entries (verified no other tenants' events; superadmin same window saw 33 users' events platform-wide); action filter works; cursor pagination works; format=csv returns text/csv attachment with header row; 403 for org member.

story: As an IdP (Okta/Entra) using an org-admin API key, I discover the SCIM capabilities.
expected: Bearer API-key auth + org-admin role; a token without an org context gets 403 {code:'scim_org_required'} — SCIM strictly requires an org-scoped admin key. Returns static SCIM 2.0 config/schema/resource-type documents.
notes: Org-admin API key returns static ServiceProviderConfig/Schemas/ResourceTypes (200); non-admin org key 403 insufficient_org_role; unauthenticated 401. No-org key state not constructible in this stack (every account has a personal org); scim_org_required guard is present in code for that case.

story: As an IdP, I list, create, read, replace, and patch users in the customer org.
expected: Org-admin key required; all operations are bounded to the key's org. List supports startIndex/count (max 100) and SCIM filter. POST returns 201 and create_or_update upserts by userName; PUT preserves userName from the existing resource; PATCH requires the SCIM PatchOp schema when schemas is supplied (400 otherwise). Mutations are committed per request.
notes: POST 201 creates SCIM user in key's org; re-POST same userName upserts to same id; list supports startIndex/count (count max 100, 101 rejected 422) and userName eq filter; GET of user outside org 404 SCIM error; PUT without userName preserves existing userName (documented setdefault behavior); PATCH with non-PatchOp schema 400; proper PatchOp toggles active.

story: As an IdP, I deprovision a user when they leave the customer's directory.
expected: Org-admin key required; DELETE is implemented as a PATCH setting active=false (soft deactivation, never a hard delete) and returns 204 with no body. Org-scoped — cannot deprovision users outside the key's org.
notes: DELETE returns 204 no body; user soft-deactivated (GET shows active:false, still retrievable - no hard delete; membership removed); cross-org delete 404.

story: As an IdP, I read and push group membership so directory groups drive org roles.
expected: Org-admin key required; groups are org-scoped, group_id accepts a path segment (:path converter). PATCH applies membership operations and commits; unknown group/org mismatch surfaces the service's error rather than crossing the tenant boundary.
notes: Groups are org-scoped role groups (role:admin/member/viewer) with members; colon path segment works; unknown group 404 SCIM error; PATCH add member moved user viewer->member (confirmed via /orgs/members).

page: Depends(admit_analysis) on POST /validate and sibling compute routes
story: As the platform, I bound in-flight analyses so a burst returns clean retryable 429s instead of DB-pool 500s, and no single org starves the rest.
expected: Beyond MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES (default 8) globally the request gets 429 {code:'server_busy'} with Retry-After; beyond MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES_PER_ORG (default 3) for the caller's org it gets 429 {code:'org_at_capacity'} with Retry-After. Slots are always released in finally even when the analysis fails. Fails OPEN (no-op) for unauthenticated callers, unresolvable membership, or a membership-lookup DB error; ADMISSION_DISABLED bypass works only outside RELEASE — in production the gate cannot be switched off.
notes: 16 concurrent STEP /validate from one org: 11x 200, 5x 429 {code:org_at_capacity} with Retry-After: 5; slots released (subsequent requests succeeded, no 500s). Counters are per-worker (4 uvicorn workers), so moderate cross-org bursts pass; global server_busy ceiling not separately triggered (would need 8+ in flight on one worker across 3+ orgs) - same gate, org path verified.

story: As an org member, I propose a DRAFT rate-card/shop-profile version for admin review.
expected: Org member+ required; 400 if caller has no org, unknown asset_type, target version not found (404), or target not in 'draft' status (400). On success creates a 'proposed' request, emits an org-scoped admin-audience notification (governance.change_requested), and returns the serialized request. Rate-limited 60/hour.
notes: Org member proposed draft -> 'proposed' request serialized; 400 unknown asset_type; 404 target version not found; 400 target not in draft status (after publish); admin notification governance.change_requested emitted (seen in admin inbox).

story: As any org member (viewer+), I browse my org's change requests and open one.
expected: Viewer role required; list is org-scoped newest-first with optional ?status filter and returns an honest empty list when the caller has no org. Detail returns 404 for a missing request, another org's request, or a caller with no org — cross-tenant reads never succeed.
notes: List org-scoped newest-first with ?status filter; other org's list honestly empty; detail 404 for missing id and for another org's request id.

story: As an org admin, I approve a proposed change, which publishes the target draft through the library's own publish path.
expected: Org-admin required; 404 unknown/cross-org request, 409 if the request is not in 'proposed' status. Publishing goes through the library's existing path — a publish failure surfaces that library error and the request is NOT marked approved (fail-closed). Success resolves the pending review notification, emits governance.approved + library.version_published audit events, and returns both the request and the published version.
notes: Non-admin 403; cross-org 404; approve published the target draft via the library path and returned {change_request approved, published_version status:published}; re-approve 409; unknown id 404; pending review notification resolved (status resolved in inbox).

story: As an org admin, I reject a proposed change with an optional note; the draft stays a draft.
expected: Org-admin required; 404 unknown/cross-org, 409 if not 'proposed'. Rejection never mutates the target draft (it remains draft, nothing published), resolves the review notification, emits governance.rejected, and returns the request in 'rejected' state with the note.
notes: Non-admin 403; reject returned status rejected with note; target draft remained status draft (verified via rate-library GET); re-reject 409; cross-org 404.

story: As any org member (viewer+), I list my org's notifications with unread/dismissed/status filters.
expected: Viewer role required; org-scoped with per-user read/dismiss state, cursor-paginated (limit 1-100). status must match open|resolved|all; default shows unread non-dismissed; 400 when dismissed=true is combined with unread=true (contradictory). A caller with no org gets an honest empty list, not an error.
notes: Org-scoped list with per-user read/dismiss state; default = open + unread non-dismissed; status must match open|resolved|all (bogus 422); dismissed=true&unread=true 400; limit 101 rejected; cursor fields present.

story: As any org member, I mark a notification read, dismiss it from my inbox, or restore a dismissed one — affecting only my own view.
expected: Viewer role required; state (read_at/dismissed_at) is per-user, org-scoped — another org's notification id is not reachable. dismiss/restore return 404 when the caller has no org; read no-ops with {ok:true}. Each returns the updated serialized notification.
notes: read/dismiss/restore each return {ok, notification} with updated per-user read_at/dismissed_at; dismissed item leaves default view and appears under dismissed=true; restore clears dismissed_at; another org's notification id 404; state is per-user (admin's read-all left other member's copy unread).

story: As any org member, I clear my unread badge in one call.
expected: Viewer role required; marks all of the caller's org notifications read for this user only and returns {ok:true, count, read_at}. No-org callers get count 0 with ok:true (honest no-op).
notes: Marks caller's open org notifications read: returned {ok:true, count:1, read_at} with an open unread present, honest {ok:true, count:0, read_at:null} otherwise (only open-status notifications counted, matching implementation); other user's unread state untouched.

story: As a security reviewer, I verify every API response carries hardening headers without breaking streaming bodies.
expected: Every HTTP response (including streamed CSV exports — pure-ASGI, not buffered) carries Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy disabling camera/mic/geolocation, and Server rewritten to 'ProofShape' (stack never advertised). SECURITY_HEADERS_ENABLED=0 disables it (default on).
error_found: Server stack IS advertised: every backend response carries TWO Server headers - 'server: uvicorn' (uvicorn's own banner) followed by 'server: ProofShape' (middleware). Expected 'Server rewritten to ProofShape (stack never advertised)'. Reproduce: curl -sD - http://127.0.0.1:8000/health | grep -i '^server' -> 'server: uvicorn' + 'server: ProofShape'. Same on authed JSON, 404s, and streamed CSV. The middleware docstring says the uvicorn banner is suppressed via --no-server-header in the process command; the running process lacks that flag.
notes: HSTS max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy camera/mic/geo disabled, single 'server: ProofShape' header - present on normal responses, 404 errors, and the streamed audit-log CSV export.

story: As an operator debugging an incident, I correlate a client request with logs and Sentry via one ID.
expected: An inbound X-Request-ID header is propagated; absent one, a UUID4 is generated. The ID is echoed back on the response as X-Request-ID, bound into structlog contextvars for every log line of the request, tagged onto the Sentry scope, and unbound after completion.
notes: Inbound X-Request-ID echoed verbatim on the response; absent one, a fresh UUID4 is generated per request (distinct across calls). Log/Sentry binding not externally observable; header contract fully verified.

page: Rate-limit + kill-switch behavior across identity/org/governance/notifications routes
story: As the platform, I throttle each route (e.g. 20/hour onboarding, 20/hour invites, 60/hour governance decisions, 120/hour reads) and gate all mutations behind the global kill-switch.
expected: Exceeding a route's slowapi limit returns 429; every mutating route in orgs/identity onboarding carries Depends(require_kill_switch_open) so writes are refused while the kill-switch is closed, while reads remain available — fail-closed for writes only.

expected: Selecting a class re-runs verification with material_class in the /validate/cost form; the provenance chip reads USER only for non-default choices (or CAD when the cost report's material_class assumption says so), else DEFAULT with copy 'uses a default material and ambient service until you declare otherwise'. The monotonic run token ensures rapid re-selection never leaves a stale material's result on screen.
notes: DEFAULT copy 'uses a default material and ambient service until you declare otherwise' before declaration; selecting Steel re-ran cost and shows 'material class steel' with ● USER provenance; rapid Aluminum->Titanium leaves 'material class titanium' displayed (monotonic run token, no stale result).

story: As a shop owner, I want my declared machines compared per-route against the part so that fit is a measured-vs-declared comparison, never a fabricated pass.
expected: Step 1 lists up to 8 machines from GET /machine-inventory with USER provenance and envelope summaries; empty floor shows 'No machines declared' with a 'Declare your floor →' CTA to the Machines screen. Only known engine process ids are forwarded as owned_processes to /validate/cost (unknown ids omitted so the call never 400s). With a verification block, RouteFitBlock renders ✓/✗/? per route with the concrete need-vs-have gap and an 'acquisition gap' line; without it, copy states 'MAKEABILITY NOT EVALUATED — no fit is faked here'. Undeclared capability renders '?', never a pass.
notes: Empty floor: step 1 shows 'No machines declared' with 'Declare your floor →' CTA that opens the Machines screen. Declared cnc_3axis 'QA VF-2' (x/y/z 762/406/508, $85/hr) + sla 'QA Mars 4' via authed proxy (unknown capability key rejected 400 server-side — catalog enforced); re-run lists both machines with USER provenance and envelope figures, per-route fit marks and acquisition language render from the verification block, and the rail rate dot fills ('Your shop rates are bound · ● SHOP').

feature: Should-cost quantity scrub with crossover and marginal rate
story: As a cost engineer, I want to scrub quantity across the engine's computed ladder so that I see make-now vs tooling economics with honest interpolation labels.
expected: The scrub reads the real 6-point ladder [1,100,1000,2000,5000,10000] (a declared annual_volume from part-context replaces the nearest interior point and becomes an exact computed point). Each readout is labelled 'engine-exact', 'interpolated between computed N and M', or 'clamped… not extrapolated'. Crossover qty from decision.crossover_qty marks the axis ('no crossover computed' otherwise). When an owned passing machine declares an hourly rate, the make-now card reads 'OWNED → MARGINAL' naming machine + $/hr with SHOP provenance. The confidence band shows the engine's real low/point/high and 'not shop-validated · n=0' when unvalidated.
notes: Default readout 'engine-exact — a computed point' at qty 100; scrubbed interior position -> 'interpolated between computed 1 and 100'; min edge stays engine-exact (real ladder point 1); 'crossover ≈ 529' marked from decision.crossover_qty; band 'assumption-based, not yet validated' with n=0. Ladder endpoints 1..10,000 rendered; annual_volume point replacement not re-exercised this pass (no program declared on the fresh org; mechanics verified in pass 1).

story: As a decision owner, I want to record make-inhouse/outside/redesign/acquire with an optional note on the saved cost-decision so that the outcome is auditable.
expected: When the cost report carries saved.id, the persisted disposition + note hydrate via GET /cost-decisions/{id}; choosing/withdrawing/noting calls setCostDecisionDisposition (PATCH) and toasts with the record short-id; failures show 'Decision controls paused — <error>. Nothing was changed.' with Retry. 'Make in-house' is disabled with an explanatory lock while route DFM is blocked. With persistence off, the choice is kept session-only and labelled '(persistence off)'. Choosing Acquire opens the acquisition modal; 'Open the record →' navigates to Records.
notes: 'Make outside' saved via PUT /api/proxy/cost-decisions/{id}/disposition with status '✓ Make outside — recorded ... saved and auditable on cost-decision #...' (PUT is the implemented method vs the story's PATCH wording — unchanged from both prior passes, same semantics); hydration GET /cost-decisions/{id} observed; note save works. Induced save outage (with the client's 2 retries exhausted) -> 'Decision controls paused — Failed to fetch. Nothing was changed.' with Retry; Retry clears the pause and controls become usable again. 'Open the record →' present.

story: As a shop owner weighing capex, I want the not-owned tooling route framed as a capital question so that I see crossover economics without invented vendor prices.
expected: Opens from the tooling card / Acquire disposition (Esc closes back to the walk). Charts only engine-computed per-quantity unit costs and decision.crossover_qty; the org ranking of 'which acquisition unlocks the most parts' loads from the capability-investment endpoint (fetchCapabilityInvestment). Standalone tool purchase price is explicitly withheld (engine produces no vendor capex); with no cost/decision/tooling route an honest empty state renders, never a fake chart.
notes: Opened from the tooling card 'Open acquisition consideration →'; modal charts only engine per-quantity unit costs with crossover/amortization economics; vendor purchase price explicitly withheld (not an engine output); org ranking fetched live from /api/proxy/catalog/capability-investment (1 request observed on open); Esc closes back to the walk.

story: As a user, I want to query the computed result ('cost drivers at qty 500', 'compare routes') so that I get deterministic engine artifacts, never generated numbers.
expected: The dock is disabled until a cost report exists ('Load a part above…'). parseAsk routes to artifacts: cost-at-qty, compare-routes (refuses when only one route was costed), compare saved decisions (live GET /cost-decisions/compare; refuses when persistence is off or only one record exists, quoting why), explain-verdict, materials, drivers, time, crossover. Any natural-language or non-deterministic ask renders a refusal artifact rather than a fabricated answer.
notes: Before any result the dock input is disabled with 'Load a part above — the engine answers only about a computed part.' After a run: 'cost drivers at qty 500' renders the drivers artifact; 'compare routes' renders the comparison; 'Compare saved decisions' with one record renders the honest refusal ('Compare needs a second saved decision — this org has just this one on record'), and with 2+ records performs a live GET /cost-decisions/compare (observed); natural-language ask and the 'An uncomputable ask' chip render refusal artifacts — no fabricated numbers.

story: As an engineer uploading a multi-part STEP assembly, I want the whole rendered in world position with per-part DFM and should-cost so that I inspect each part in context.
expected: STEP/IGES with >=2 solids goes to POST /validate/assembly?format=json (structured model) and ?format=glb (combined render); the single-part /validate/cost path is skipped so no spurious 400 flashes. The heavier per-part analysis (fetchAssemblyAnalysis, ~15s) then populates rows with tree-counted quantity (FACT), DFM verdict, and unit cost — 'analysing per-part…' shown honestly while in flight; a part that fails analysis shows its own error, never a fabricated figure. Selecting a part highlights it on the stage with name + tree path; a new upload revokes the old GLB and run-token guards stale merges. Single solids stay on the unchanged single-part path.
notes: as1-tu-203.stp (AS1 assembly): POST /validate/assembly?format=json + ?format=glb + ?format=analysis ran; no single-part /validate/cost fired at upload (no spurious 400). 'ANALYSING PER-PART — running DFM + should-cost on every solid' shown honestly in flight; 18 product-tree rows with full tree paths and tree-counted quantities (·2/·3) populated with per-part DFM verdicts and unit costs ($) when analysis completed. Row click highlights on stage ('◆ selected plate · as1/PLATE/plate'). Single-solid qa-cube.step is probed (format=json classifies single_part by design) then stays on the single-part path — no assembly panel, normal verdict walk completes.

story: As a program manager, I want a part's declared lineage (program → assembly → part, units/parent) on the stage so that I see where it lives — or that it has no home yet.
expected: After a run, GET /part-context/{mesh_hash} hydrates the stage context card (testid verify-stage-context): declared parent shows the lineage path and 'N / parent' pill; a 404 is not an error — the card shows 'orphan until declared'; a genuine read failure shows a 'context read failed' pill. A declared annual_volume also reshapes the cost quantity ladder on the next run.
notes: GET /part-context/{sha256} hydrates verify-stage-context after the run; undeclared parent renders 'CONTEXT · not declared · no parent assembly declared · orphan until declared' — the honest orphan state, no false error pill. Ladder mechanics re-verified in VER-013.

story: As a librarian of parts, I want the org's closest prior part suggested with real confidence so that I can confirm identity without the system asserting it as fact.
expected: A grounded identity riding the cost report renders a suggestion card (confidence % + bucket, runner-ups, RETRIEVED provenance); confirming POSTs /identity/confirm with the part's mesh_hash and toasts 'saved to your part library'; 'Not this' dismisses reversibly and offers manual declaration. A non-grounded-but-close match renders a softer low-confidence card; an empty/anonymous corpus renders nothing at all. Confirm without a mesh hash errors 're-verify to confirm'.
notes: Corpus retrieval demonstrably runs: uploading qa-part2.stl in an org with prior parts rendered the honest line 'No confident match in your part library yet — geometry retrieved 1 prior part, none confident enough to suggest.' — retrieval executed and no identity card was fabricated below the confidence bar; a truly empty fresh org renders nothing at all, per the story. No upload reached the grounded-confident bar live, so the /identity/confirm POST path was not reachable this pass (same as prior retest).

feature: Design Studio STEP handoff with integrity check
story: As a Design Studio user, I want my generated STEP revision to import and verify automatically so that the artifact takes the same untrusted path as a manual upload.
expected: ?design=<26-char id>(&revision=N) fetches /api/proxy/designs/{id}/download.step (or /revisions/{N}/download.step), enforces the 100 MB limit, rejects empty bodies, and verifies the SHA-256 of the bytes against the x-geometry-sha256 header before running the normal verification. A status banner walks loading → running → ready (dismissible); invalid ids/revisions or any failure show role=alert with the exact reason and a 'Return to Design Studio' link. Import requires an active organization.
notes: Fresh design (plate 80x60x5, 2 holes) generated to ready; /verify?design=<id> fetched download.step, banner walked importing -> 'Verification finished', the normal pipeline ran, and the on-page Evidence hash equals the revision geometry_hash (47c2ea1b...9613) — integrity verified. Tampered x-geometry-sha256 (route-injected) -> 'The generated STEP artifact failed its integrity check.'; invalid id -> 'That Design Studio link is invalid.' (role=alert + Return to Design Studio); invalid revision -> 'That design revision is invalid.'; nonexistent id -> 'The design artifact is not ready (404).'

feature: Home dashboard with honest unavailable/empty states
story: As a returning user, I want a desk of real org data (records, floor, reviews, ground truth) so that loading failures are never presented as empty results.

Any failure raises a role=alert 'Couldn't load <sources>… nothing is being presented as an empty result' with a 'Retry organization data' button, and the affected KPI reads 'RETRY NEEDED'; true empties show dashed empty states ('Nothing in flight', 'n=0 · every band still hatched'). The calibrated-estimates KPI stays permanently withheld ('—') because no list summary can derive it. Start-here grid offers drop/browse CAD (drag-drop supported), guided example, and Design Studio link.
notes: Fresh org: dashed empty states, 'n=0 · every band still hatched' ground truth, calibrated KPI permanently withheld ('— CALIBRATED ESTIMATES · NO DATA'), start-here grid with drop/browse CAD + guided example + Design Studio link. Aborting cost-decisions + machine-inventory -> role=alert "Couldn't load records, machine inventory... nothing is being presented as an empty result" with 'Retry organization data'; KPIs read 'RETRY NEEDED'; retry restores the data.

notes: Hotkeys 8/8 (h/v/p/r/g/m/t/c -> home/verify/catalog/records/programs/machines/triage/calibration, verified via the workspace-section select value); '?' opens the shortcuts sheet; Ctrl+K opens the palette, typing in it never triggers nav, Esc closes; ?screen=records deep-links; rate dot hollow on a rate-less org ('no shop rate bound yet') and filled once an $85/hr machine exists ('Your shop rates are bound · ● SHOP'); mobile select replaces tabs at 700px.
